parsed.explanation: The combined regime documents state-directed targeting: national-authority police arresting and torturing queer residents (usually on collaboration charges), two explicit homosexuality prosecutions in an undated three-year window, and an official ban on LGBTQ activity followed by hate campaigns. One region's contested 1936 ordinance carries 10–14 years; the other region decriminalised only by inheritance, not domestic law. No legal gender recognition, no non-discrimination statute, and unnamed treaty non-signatory status leave no remedy. Social acceptance is very low (rank 130, flat 2010–2020) and ~90 LGBT residents fled violence. All key items are undated; no trans-specific rate exists. Absence of entry, facility and detention-placement data is not safety. Extrapolation from criminalisation plus documented police torture plus absent recourse resolves low.

entry_documents.exposure: Entry procedure, passport gender markers, airport or checkpoint screening, and device searches are explicitly not sourced. Marker mismatch friction can be neither confirmed nor excluded.
entry_documents.protection: No documented acceptance of foreign X/diverse markers or chosen-name documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Undocumented border practice could route a discrepant document into the same police apparatus documented as arresting and torturing queer residents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National-authority police documented arresting and torturing gay residents, usually via collaboration charges; two people tried explicitly for homosexuality in an undated three-year window. Contested 1936 ordinance carries up to 10–14 years in one region.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented habeas, consular access, anti-torture remedy, or effective challenge; source notes inability to be openly gay in national-authority areas.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any document mismatch, service refusal or street incident that brings police involvement enters this same custody pathway.

care_services.exposure: ART interrupted for HIV-positive queer people due to limited medication and high stigma; only 98 registered cases 1988–2017 acknowledged as a large undercount; blockaded region's health system collapsed from October 2023, making life-saving HIV medication especially hard to obtain.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care or hospitalisation could out a visitor into a hostile policing environment while care is unavailable.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police banned LGBTQ activity by a queer cultural organisation, triggering a hate-message wave activists called a serious threat; police increasingly enforced Islamic law after an uprising; queer people blackmailed into informant roles by neighbouring-state security.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No documented protective protocol, hate-crime provision, or police training.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing compounds private hostility: reporting an incident risks engaging the perpetrators.

minors_guardians.exposure: Family and social persecution documented as harsher than formal law; twelve lesbian/bisexual/queer women reported public and family abuse (2018, women-only sample). No minor-specific or travelling-family evidence.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling adult with a minor risks family-style outing dynamics, but the record cannot establish specifics.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Periodic transphobic threats and attacks reported with no dates or counts; ~90 LGBT residents fled violence to a neighbouring jurisdiction; social acceptance ranked 130th, nearly unchanged 2010–2020.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Regional cross-border advocacy and monitoring exist, but operate largely from a neighbouring state; no domestic enforcement record.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street hostility meets a police apparatus documented as hostile rather than protective.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No legal gender recognition, no broad LGBTIQ+ non-discrimination protections, national authority legislated neither for nor against, unsigned key treaties unnamed, 2003 draft code status unknown, 1936 ordinance's force contested, all incident dates missing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Bare legality of trans identity as such in both regions; one region's code contains no consensual-sex offence.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: With no statutory complaint to invoke, every other exposure terminates without recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in structure: state harassment, repeated custody, scarce legal aid, incomplete records. Lower than this dossier, because its courts overturned some convictions and its penalties were fines, whereas here police torture is documented, penalties reach 10–14 years, and no remedy or oversight appears at all.

Higher than this dossier. Karthovia's stops end in release without charge, with courts formally accepting complaints. Here the state tortures people in custody, criminalisation carries a decade-plus, an official ban exists, and no functioning remedy is documented — worse on both severity and recourse.

Lower than this dossier. Oskara has organised morality sweeps, coerced statements, a credibly-tied capital clause and consistent recourse failure. Here prosecution is rare (two cases, undated), no death penalty is mentioned, and one region is decriminalised — state torture pulls it down but not to that tier.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a split regime: one region inherited decriminalisation, the other carries a contested 1936 code with 10–14 years, and practice accounts show national-authority police arresting and torturing queer people regardless of the formal text. Outing therefore routes into a custody apparatus documented as a perpetrator, with no legal-gender-recognition route, no non-discrimination complaint, unnamed treaty gaps and an official ban on LGBTQ organising. Very low, flat social acceptance and documented flight of ~90 LGBT residents corroborate hostility. Because every incident is undated, no trans-specific rate exists, and entry, facility and detention-placement rules are unsourced, the low score rests on structural extrapolation — criminalisation plus state torture plus absent remedy — not on proven frequency.
